BACKPORT: VSOCK: use TCP state constants for sk_state There are two state fields: socket->state and sock->sk_state. The socket->state field uses SS_UNCONNECTED, SS_CONNECTED, etc while the sock->sk_state typically uses values that match TCP state constants (TCP_CLOSE, TCP_ESTABLISHED). AF_VSOCK does not follow this convention and instead uses SS_* constants for both fields. The sk_state field will be exposed to userspace through the vsock_diag interface for ss(8), netstat(8), and other programs. This patch switches sk_state to TCP state constants so that the meaning of this field is consistent with other address families. Not just AF_INET and AF_INET6 use the TCP constants, AF_UNIX and others do too. The following mapping was used to convert the code: SS_FREE -> TCP_CLOSE SS_UNCONNECTED -> TCP_CLOSE SS_CONNECTING -> TCP_SYN_SENT SS_CONNECTED -> TCP_ESTABLISHED SS_DISCONNECTING -> TCP_CLOSING VSOCK_SS_LISTEN -> TCP_LISTEN In __vsock_create() the sk_state initialization was dropped because sock_init_data() already initializes sk_state to TCP_CLOSE. BACKPORT: VSOCK: use TCP state constants for sk_state There are two state fields: socket->state and sock->sk_state. The socket->state field uses SS_UNCONNECTED, SS_CONNECTED, etc while the sock->sk_state typically uses values that match TCP state constants (TCP_CLOSE, TCP_ESTABLISHED). AF_VSOCK does not follow this convention and instead uses SS_* constants for both fields. The sk_state field will be exposed to userspace through the vsock_diag interface for ss(8), netstat(8), and other programs. This patch switches sk_state to TCP state constants so that the meaning of this field is consistent with other address families. Not just AF_INET and AF_INET6 use the TCP constants, AF_UNIX and others do too. The following mapping was used to convert the code: SS_FREE -> TCP_CLOSE SS_UNCONNECTED -> TCP_CLOSE SS_CONNECTING -> TCP_SYN_SENT SS_CONNECTED -> TCP_ESTABLISHED SS_DISCONNECTING -> TCP_CLOSING VSOCK_SS_LISTEN -> TCP_LISTEN In __vsock_create() the sk_state initialization was dropped because sock_init_data() already initializes sk_state to TCP_CLOSE. FIXUP: FROMLIST: ASoC: SOF: Add Sound Open Firmware driver core If CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF=y and CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=m, builds fail with ld: sound/soc/sof/core.o: in function `sof_machine_check': >> sound/soc/sof/core.c:269: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' ld: sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.o: in function `sof_acpi_probe': >> sound/soc/sof/sof-acpi-dev.c:220: undefined reference to `sof_nocodec_setup' This happens because sof_nocodec_setup() is called from code built into the kernel but resides in a module. Since sof_nocodec_setup() is called unconditionally from the SOF core if CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_FORCE_NOCODEC_MODE=y, SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC must be built into the kernel if SND_SOC_SOF=y. Add the necessary dependency. sof_nocodec_setup() is called from sof-acpi-dev.c:sof_acpi_probe() if CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_FORCE_NOCODEC_MODE=y. This results in the second build failure if SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=m and SND_SOC_SOF_ACPI=y. Since we force SND_SOC_SOF_NOCODEC=y if SND_SOC_SOF=y, and SND_SOC_SOF is selected by SND_SOC_SOF_ACPI, this problem is solved with the above change as well. This change does not affect existing Chrome OS configurations and thus does not have functional impact on shipping images. tast: Remove -checktestdeps=auto flag value. -checktestdeps controls the behavior to skip tests by checking software dependencies. Formerly the flag had three values: always, never, auto. The auto value, which was actually the default when the flag is not explicitly specified, indicates that software deps should be checked if and only if tests are specified by attribute expressions (e.g. "(!disabled)") rather than exact names (e.g. "arc.Boot") or globs (e.g. "arc.*"). Since this behavior is confusing, this CL changes the flag to accept a boolean value, and sets the default to always checking software dependencies. It might be better to avoid putting these constants here at all, but for now, it seems like we should be resilient to, for example, another test (network_WiFi_BgscanBackoff?) not resetting parameters properly. Also note that WifiProxy.configure_bgscan() is really telling *shill* what to do, which indirectly also affects wpa_supplicant bgscan parameters, but shill also schedules scanning of its own. I believe this affects tests like network_WiFi_ChannelHop, which rely on the timing of re-scan attempts after the AP goes away. Funny enough, that's pretty much why the change in https://crrev.com/c/206927 was made -- to help improve the latency for detecting rebooted APs.
